images.author: Cony photos
images.why: 3927 × 2945 photograph from Caquena, Chile; source identifies Parinacota and Pomerape, with snowy peaks and clear blue sky. Wider landscape option requiring a crop centred on Parinacota.

images.source: NASA/JSC Gateway to Astronaut Photography of Earth
images.author: ISS Expedition 29 crew / NASA Johnson Space Center
images.why: 4288 × 2848 unannotated original. NASA explicitly identifies Parinacota’s symmetrical snowy cone and summit crater, with Pomerape and the surrounding lakes providing context; strong oblique-view alternative.

images.author: ISS Expedition 69 crew / NASA Johnson Space Center
images.why: 2916 × 1944 unannotated photograph. Early-evening illumination casts long shadows across the snowy twin volcanoes; NASA distinguishes Parinacota by its circular crater and intact cone. Overhead alternative suited to a crater-centred crop.

images.source: NASA/JSC Gateway to Astronaut Photography of Earth
images.author: ISS Expedition 29 crew / NASA Johnson Space Center
images.why: 4288 × 2848 unannotated original, explicitly catalogued by NASA as Cerro Pular, snow and salt lake. A 54-degree oblique photograph offering regional volcanic-landscape context; requires a crop around Pular.
